title: Yunluo
summary: The yunluo is a frame of ten small flat gongs, each tuned to its own note, hung in three rows. Held or set on a stand, it is struck with a small mallet and gives a bright, silvery tune.
howToPlay: Ten gongs are lit in three rows: the low notes at the bottom, the high ones at the top.
Strike the gong a closing ring marks. It swings and shimmers.
Moving up the frame climbs in pitch.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The gongs are small enough to hang close together, so a single player can reach every note. Its bright tone is often heard in folk ensembles and opera bands.
credits: Tradition: the yunluo of China; patterns written for this game
